facts.question: What color can the sky glow near the Sun at sunset on Mars?
facts.fact: Mars can have a blue twilight glow close to the setting Sun.
facts.explanation: Fine dust in Mars’s thin atmosphere scatters light in a way that keeps blue light concentrated near the Sun. The rest of the sky can look more yellow or orange.

source.title: What Do Sunrises and Sunsets Look Like on Mars?

facts.wonderQuestion: If you could watch one sunset anywhere in the solar system, where would you go?

facts.question: Which lasts longer on Venus: one spin of the planet or one trip around the Sun?
facts.fact: A Venus day, measured by one full spin, is longer than a Venus year.
facts.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once, but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun. Its slow spin also makes the Sun rise in the west.
facts.wonderQuestion: How would calendars work if a planet’s day were longer than its year?

facts.question: Which planet has an average density lower than water?
facts.fact: Saturn is the only planet in our solar system with an average density lower than water.
facts.explanation: That makes the familiar thought experiment true in principle: Saturn could float in a bathtub large enough to hold it. It is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.
facts.wonderQuestion: What would a realistic bathtub big enough for a planet need to be made of?

facts.question: About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
facts.fact: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
facts.explanation: Light travels incredibly fast, but space is so vast that even sunlight needs several minutes to cross the gap between the Sun and Earth.
facts.wonderQuestion: When you look at the Sun, what are you learning about its past?

facts.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
facts.fact: An octopus has three hearts.
facts.explanation: Two hearts move blood past the gills. A third circulates oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body, and it stops beating while the octopus swims.
facts.wonderQuestion: What might explain why an octopus prefers crawling to swimming?

facts.question: Which animal is known for producing cube-shaped droppings?
facts.fact: Wombats produce cube-shaped droppings.
facts.explanation: Researchers found that different parts of a wombat’s intestine stretch unevenly, shaping the material into cubes. The shape may help the droppings stay put as scent markers.
facts.wonderQuestion: What useful job could an unusual body shape quietly do?

facts.question: Which appeared first in Earth’s history: sharks or trees?
options: They appeared at about the same time
facts.fact: Sharks are older than the first trees.
facts.explanation: Shark ancestors appeared hundreds of millions of years ago. The earliest recognizable trees came later, so sharks were already in the oceans before forests existed.

source.title: Respect: Sharks Are Older than Trees

facts.wonderQuestion: What would Earth have looked like before forests existed?

facts.question: How do parrotfish help make some tropical beach sand?
options: They grind coral as they feed
Their scales break down in the sun
facts.fact: Parrotfish can turn bits of reef into fine white sand as they feed.
facts.explanation: They scrape algae from reef surfaces and also grind some of the hard calcium-carbonate material. They digest the algae and pass the crushed mineral material as sand.
facts.wonderQuestion: What else in nature is made from the leftovers of another creature’s meal?

facts.question: What do camels store in their humps?
facts.fact: A camel’s hump stores fat, not water.
facts.explanation: The fat is an energy reserve. Camels conserve water in other ways, which is why the hump myth can sound plausible even though the hump itself is not a water tank.

source.title: Everyday Mysteries: How Much Water Does a Camel’s Hump Hold?

facts.wonderQuestion: What common belief would you most like to check against the evidence?

facts.question: Botanically speaking, black-eyed peas belong to which group?
facts.fact: Black-eyed peas are a type of bean, specifically a cowpea.
facts.explanation: The everyday names for foods do not always match their botanical family. Black-eyed peas are legumes in the cowpea group.
facts.wonderQuestion: Which other foods might have names that mislead us about what they are?

facts.question: What is the scientific consensus about two large snow crystals being identical?
facts.fact: It is extraordinarily unlikely for two large, complex snow crystals to be identical in both structure and appearance.
facts.explanation: Temperature and other conditions shift as a crystal falls, shaping its branching pattern. Very simple crystals can look alike, but matching the full structure of two large crystals is vanishingly unlikely.

source.title: Is It True That No Two Snow Crystals Are Alike?

facts.wonderQuestion: How do scientists talk carefully about a claim that is almost impossible to test completely?

facts.question: Earth’s English name comes mainly from which source?
facts.fact: Earth is the only planet whose English name does not come from Greek or Roman mythology.
facts.explanation: The name comes from Old English and Germanic words for ground or soil. The other planets’ English names are tied to Roman gods and goddesses.
facts.wonderQuestion: What does the name of your home planet say about how people first understood it?

facts.question: How long is one day on Saturn?
facts.fact: A day on Saturn lasts about 10.7 Earth hours.
facts.explanation: Saturn spins quickly, completing one rotation in less than half an Earth day. Its year, by contrast, lasts about 29.4 Earth years.
facts.wonderQuestion: Would a shorter day make your daily routine feel faster or simply different?

facts.question: On Venus, which direction does the Sun rise?
facts.fact: The Sun rises in the west on Venus.
facts.explanation: Venus spins backward compared with most planets, including Earth. That retrograde rotation reverses the apparent direction of sunrise and sunset.
facts.wonderQuestion: How much of what feels like ‘up’, ‘down’, ‘east’, or ‘west’ depends on where we stand?

facts.question: Which planet is hotter at its surface: Mercury or Venus?
facts.fact: Venus is hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
facts.explanation: Venus’s thick atmosphere traps heat in a powerful greenhouse effect. Its surface reaches about 467°C (872°F).
facts.wonderQuestion: How can an atmosphere change the temperature of an entire world?

facts.question: What mainly causes Earth’s seasons?
options: Earth getting much closer to the Sun in summer
facts.fact: Earth’s seasons come mainly from the tilt of its axis.
facts.explanation: As Earth orbits the Sun, each hemisphere tilts toward or away from sunlight for part of the year. Earth is actually closest to the Sun during Northern Hemisphere winter.
facts.wonderQuestion: Why might the same month feel like a different season in another hemisphere?

facts.question: Why do we add a leap day about every four years?
options: A year is about a quarter day longer than 365 days
Earth stops rotating for one day
The Moon adds an extra orbit
facts.fact: Earth takes about 365.25 days to orbit the Sun, so calendars add a leap day to stay aligned.
facts.explanation: That extra quarter day accumulates. Adding a day every four years keeps calendar dates from drifting too far from the seasons over time.
facts.wonderQuestion: What would happen to birthdays and seasons if calendars ignored the leftover quarter day?

facts.question: Why can twilight linger unusually long on Mars?
options: The planet stops spinning at dusk
facts.fact: Dust high in Mars’s atmosphere can scatter sunlight around the planet’s horizon, extending twilight.
facts.explanation: NASA notes that the glow can remain visible for up to two hours before sunrise or after sunset, fainter as time passes.

source.title: What Do Sunrises and Sunsets Look Like on Mars?

facts.wonderQuestion: How could a long twilight change the feeling of a day on another planet?

facts.question: What do parrotfish scrape from coral while feeding?
facts.fact: Parrotfish scrape algae from reef surfaces, and grind some coral material in the process.
facts.explanation: The fish are after algae, but their beak-like teeth also wear down hard reef material. This process helps create sediment and sand in reef environments.
facts.wonderQuestion: Can an animal reshape its habitat just by eating?

facts.question: About how fast is the Moon moving away from Earth?
facts.fact: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth by about 3.8 centimeters per year.
facts.explanation: The Moon's gravity raises ocean tides, and the moving tidal bulges transfer a little of Earth's rotational energy to the Moon, nudging it into a wider orbit.
facts.wonderQuestion: How can a small change repeated for millions of years reshape the solar system?

facts.question: How is Uranus unusually tilted as it orbits the Sun?
options: It spins nearly on its side
facts.fact: Uranus is tilted so dramatically that it appears to roll around the Sun on its side.
facts.explanation: Its rotation axis is tilted about 98 degrees relative to its orbit. This extreme tilt gives the planet unusually long, intense seasons.
facts.wonderQuestion: What would seasons feel like if your world had decades of daylight followed by decades of darkness?

facts.question: How many sunrises can astronauts on the ISS see in one Earth day?
facts.fact: The International Space Station circles Earth roughly every 90 minutes, giving its crew about 16 sunrises and sunsets each day.
facts.explanation: At orbital speed, the station repeatedly moves from Earth's sunlit side into its shadow and back again. The crew uses a shared time standard to keep daily schedules steady.

source.title: Frequently Asked Questions: Spot The Station

facts.wonderQuestion: Would seeing sixteen sunrises a day make time feel different to you?

facts.question: Where has spacecraft evidence found water ice on Mercury?
options: In sunlit plains near the equator
Inside permanently shadowed craters near the poles
Floating in clouds above the planet
facts.fact: Mercury has water ice in some permanently shadowed craters near its poles.
facts.explanation: Although Mercury is close to the Sun, some crater floors never receive direct sunlight and stay cold enough for ice to persist.

source.title: NASA Spacecraft Finds New Mercury Water Ice Evidence

facts.wonderQuestion: What other surprising places might preserve water by staying in permanent shadow?

facts.question: What did Apollo astronauts leave behind that detected moonquakes?
facts.fact: Instruments left by Apollo astronauts recorded moonquakes, including some that lasted more than ten minutes.
facts.explanation: Some quakes are linked to the pull of Earth's gravity; others happen as the Moon cools and contracts. Lunar quakes can last longer than many earthquakes because the Moon is dry and fractured differently from Earth.
facts.wonderQuestion: How might the same shaking behave differently on a dry, airless world?

facts.question: What gives flamingos their pink color?
options: A pink pigment in their skin from birth
Pigments in the food they eat
facts.fact: Flamingos get their pink color from pigments in their food.
facts.explanation: Carotenoids in algae and tiny crustaceans are processed by the flamingo's body and contribute to the color of its feathers.
facts.wonderQuestion: What other colors in nature might come from an animal's menu?

facts.question: Which body part do butterflies use to taste?
facts.fact: Butterflies can taste with sensors on their feet.
facts.explanation: When a butterfly lands on a plant, taste sensors on its feet help it assess the surface. That can help a female find a suitable plant for laying eggs.

source.title: 8 Reasons to Be in Awe of Pollinators

facts.wonderQuestion: How would your choices change if you could taste everything you touched?

facts.question: How do dolphins rest while still coming up to breathe?
options: They rest one half of the brain at a time
They stop needing oxygen while asleep
facts.fact: Dolphins can sleep with one brain hemisphere resting while the other stays alert.
facts.explanation: This unihemispheric sleep lets them keep swimming and surface to breathe. They can also keep one eye open while the opposite side of the brain is more alert.

source.title: 11 Cool Facts About Whales, Dolphins, and Porpoises

facts.wonderQuestion: What would it feel like to wake up only halfway?

facts.question: Where can a sea otter stash food while diving?
options: In a shell tucked under its tail
In loose skin pockets under its forearms
facts.fact: Sea otters have loose skin pockets under their forearms where they can stash prey during a dive.
facts.explanation: The pockets leave an otter's paws free to keep hunting. Some otters also carry a favorite rock there to use as a tool for opening shellfish.
facts.wonderQuestion: What small feature would make your everyday tasks easier if you had it?

facts.question: How old might some Greenland sharks be, according to scientific estimates?
facts.fact: Some Greenland sharks may live for several centuries; one study estimated the oldest shark examined at 272 to 512 years old.
facts.explanation: Those are estimates, not exact birth dates. Researchers used radiocarbon dating of proteins in the sharks' eye lenses, and the method has uncertainty.

source.title: How Long Do Greenland Sharks Live?

facts.wonderQuestion: What could a shark alive for centuries have witnessed in the ocean?

facts.question: What can an axolotl regrow after an injury?
options: Limbs and several other body parts
facts.fact: Axolotls can regenerate limbs and other structures, including parts of the spinal cord and heart.
facts.explanation: Scientists study how these salamanders rebuild complex body parts to better understand tissue repair. Their abilities are remarkable, but they are not simply immune to injury or illness.
facts.wonderQuestion: What might scientists learn by comparing healing across different animals?

facts.question: What can a honeybee communicate with its waggle dance?
options: The direction and distance of a food source
A warning that rain will arrive
facts.fact: A honeybee's waggle dance can tell other bees the direction and distance of a newly found food source.
facts.explanation: Scout bees return to the nest and move in a pattern that gives other workers useful information about where to forage.

source.title: The Why, What, When, Where, Who, How of Pollination

facts.wonderQuestion: What information would you try to encode in a dance if you could not use words?

facts.question: Roughly how many geysers are found in Yellowstone National Park?
facts.fact: Yellowstone has more than 500 geysers among its thousands of hydrothermal features.
facts.explanation: Geysers are rare hot springs with narrow underground passages that let pressure build until water and steam erupt. Yellowstone contains the largest concentration of active geysers on Earth.
facts.wonderQuestion: What hidden underground conditions have to line up for a geyser to erupt?

facts.question: How can low-intensity fires help giant sequoias reproduce?
options: They make the trees grow new roots overnight
They turn the bark into seeds
Heat helps open cones and release seeds
facts.fact: Heat from low-intensity fires can help open giant sequoia cones and release seeds.
facts.explanation: Fire can also clear space and expose soil where seedlings can take root. Much hotter, severe fires can damage or destroy the cones and threaten the trees instead.
facts.wonderQuestion: How can the same force in nature help an ecosystem in one form and harm it in another?

facts.question: How much water falls on one square mile during one inch of rain?
facts.fact: One inch of rain over one square mile amounts to about 17.4 million gallons of water.
facts.explanation: A thin layer spread over a large area adds up quickly. NOAA uses this example to show why even modest rainfall can move a huge volume of water through a watershed.

source.title: How Much Water Is in That Cloud?

facts.wonderQuestion: Where does all that rainwater go after it hits a city or a forest?

facts.question: During migration, how far can monarch butterflies travel in a day?
facts.fact: Monarch butterflies can travel up to about 30 miles in a day during migration.
facts.explanation: Their long journey depends on weather, winds, and the availability of stopover habitat. Generations of monarchs take part in the broader migration cycle.

source.title: The Why, What, When, Where, Who, How of Pollination

facts.wonderQuestion: What would you need to plan for a journey that spans thousands of miles over several generations?

facts.question: What can create vivid color bands around some Yellowstone hot springs?
facts.fact: Heat-loving microorganisms can form colorful mats in Yellowstone's hydrothermal areas.
facts.explanation: Different microbes thrive under different conditions, and dense communities can appear as bands of color around hot water and mineral deposits.
facts.wonderQuestion: What might life look like in a place that seems too extreme for anything to survive?
